name: Leader Flags
promise: One surprising ranking between countries, drawn from real data and animated so you can watch it change.
audience: Adults 18-45 who like maps, data and country rivalry; global audience.

benchmarks.study: Countryball rankings (re-edits of other creators' work). We make original data episodes.

voice.name: Felix (Fish Audio library, Australian male)
voice.notes: Fish free tier: 50 requests/day across ALL channels. One request per paragraph, cached by hash. User picked Kokoro George (bm_george) on 2026-10-06 as the voice while there is no Fish key.

look.texture: clean flat bars, round flag badges with faces, subtle paper grain

captions.style: Anton, uppercase, 2-5 words per chunk, white with ink outline

safe_zone.note: px at 1080x1920; keep text out of the platform UI (title, buttons, progress bar)

look.notes: Flags from a public-domain flag set, redrawn in code. Every chart shows its data source on screen.

series.name: Race through time

beats: hook: the surprising leader in year one

example_titles: Canada vs Russia: who is actually colder?

script.tone: Dry sports-commentator deadpan over the data.
rules: One idea per line. Short sentences. Deadpan: state absurd facts plainly and let the gap carry the joke.
Line one is the hook: the most surprising true sentence in the episode, under the word limit, no preamble.
Spell numbers the way they are spoken ('nineteen thirty-two', 'ten thousand'). Put the digits in the captions.
Every line with a fact, number, name or date cites dossier claim ids. Jokes may not smuggle in new facts.
Estimates and self-reported numbers carry their label on screen (e.g. 'the major's own count').
The last line calls back to the hook or loops into it, so a replay feels intentional.
Use 'gap' (seconds of silence after a line) for comic timing: 0.4-0.6 s before a punchline.
Every ranked number comes from one dataset file stored in the episode (data/*.csv) with its source URL and year.
Name the metric precisely (GDP per capita, PPP, current international $) on screen.

radar: New dataset releases (World Bank WDI, UN population prospects, FAO, IMF WEO)
Our World in Data grapher charts
Sporting and global events (Olympics medal tables)
avoid: Rankings that invite ethnic or religious hostility
Metrics without a clear, current, citable dataset

preferred: Our World in Data (cite its underlying source)
sources.notes: Datasets are downloaded into the episode folder with the source URL and access date.

tracks.caption: upbeat sports broadcast underscore, driving drums, staccato brass, synth bass, competitive, instrumental
light tension game-show underscore, ticking hi-hat, pizzicato, piano stabs, instrumental
punchy countdown underscore, tight drums, synth stabs, rising tension, modern, instrumental
triumphant winner reveal, big brass fanfare, bright synth arpeggios, celebratory, instrumental

rotation.policy: one track per channel until the analytics stage has 5 uploads with it; then try the next track for 5 uploads and keep whichever has the better average view duration (YouTube Analytics averageViewPercentage). Record each switch in docs/DECISIONS.md.
